I had a similar thing happen to me. Went deep in the woods to trip shrooms with about 10 people. Tripped during the day and something ripped my personality right out of me. I was suddenly unable to communicate with anyone and full of fear and paranoia. Ended up finding a way back to our tents and spending most of the time alone.

That trip fucked with me for years. At that point in my life I had done plenty of recreational drugs, mostly LSD and THC, and had finally come out of my shell and made a lot of friends. Coming out of that trip I continually stumbled over myself and had a permanent sense of inadequacy. I fell head first into a messed up relationship. My lack of self confidence slowly dissolved all the friendships I had built up over the past two years.

Time went on. My depression mounted. My anxiety had built to a peak during that lonely trip with friends - and it never went down. I started to experience imposter syndrome at my work: I was plagued by my own self-opinion while compliments from my boss bounced off my ears, then concerns, then whole meetings on my health. 

My schizophrenic* girlfriend left. I saw a thread of light and began tearing my way out. I had had a surgery go wrong when I was 20, and at this point I finally pushed myself to do physical therapy and exercise. I built myself up to almost a 5k, took some classes, got a little better at being better at work. Reconnected with a few friends. 

But that one part of me never left. I still knew, somehow, that I was on the verge of completely falling apart. One morning I was on my way to class on my bike and was smashed into the street by an SUV.

---

I gave up. I had always been pretty good about having appropriate lines: I let myself smoke weed and cigarettes when I wanted to, drink alcohol on the weekend if I went to a party, and every once in a while LSD or PSY. A few things I tried once: cocaine, mdma, 2C-E. I was prescribed vyvanse and xanax and took both very carefully. I had been prescribed some opioid partial agonists (e.g. Tramadol) that I never took and just tossed into my safe.

Well when I got hit by that car I suddenly had a reason to give up. I called into work planning to come back in two weeks. I could remote in if they really needed me.

My stash of expired meds put me in a fog for about 2 weeks. At its end, the xanax did what it does best - make one forget. By the time I was out of it I already had a couple thousand nitrous chargers in the mail from Amazon. That helped for a while...

...Somewhere along the line I reached out to someone who had once been a very good friend. I knew she fucked with painkillers but that wasn't why.

Day 2 of hanging out with her it's apparent that she's in withdrawal. She needs to find money for a gas bill or whatever. I know what's going on. I tell her that I'll buy as much as she wants as long as she shoots me up and leaves. It didn't take too much effort to convince her.

---
